name: Right-wing antiglobalism
summary: Right-wing antiglobalism opposes 'globalism': free trade, supranational bodies such as the UN, WTO and EU, open borders and the cosmopolitan elite it blames for them. It defends national sovereignty, tariffs and protection for domestic workers, immigration limits and a shared national culture, and casts politics as the nation and its ordinary people against a globalist elite. Scholars describe it as thin, defined by what it opposes, with conspiracist strands at its edge.
scope: The mainstream contemporary antiglobalist right in the US and Europe, scoped on opposition to globalisation: sovereignty over supranational bodies, trade protection, migration control and national identity. Built from Buchanan's The Great Betrayal, Trump's UN, convention and inaugural speeches, Orbán's 2016 speech, Hawley's 2019 NatCon speech and the scholarship on anti-globalism, with the Birch Society as lineage only. Positions the wider right holds on other issues (climate, energy, elections, military strength, taxes, family) are left null unless the doctrine's own sources state them as part of the antiglobalist case; left-wing antiglobalism and conspiracist extremes are excluded.
